newsitem.title: CANADA: TimberWest attracts U.S., Canadian bidders.
newsitem.headline: TimberWest attracts U.S., Canadian bidders.

text.p: Several potential bidders are interested in TimberWest Forest Ltd including Canadian and U.S. buyers and a final deal for the lumber producer is likely by mid-December, an official said Thursday.

Stephen Bellringer, chief executive of BC Gas and a director of TimberWest, said in an interview that the independent committee overseeing the sale hopes to announce a deal around the week of December 16.
He declined to reveal the exact number of potential buyers that would be conducting due diligence on TimberWest over the coming weeks.
"We purposely haven't given that number, but all I can say is it's several," Bellringer said. Interest has emerged from both within Canada and outside.
"There's certainly interest from the United States," he said.
When binding bids are made around December 13, the committee will compare them and then "probably target negotiations with the lead bidder at point," he said.
Those talks would seek to finalize closing details with the aim of announcing a deal around the next week, he said.

TimberWest is 52 percent owned by Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd which in turn is majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd. TimberWest was wholly owned by Fletcher Canada until 1993 when it was spun off as part of a move by Fletcher to focus on paper.

TimberWest, one of Canada's biggest public companies operating exclusively in the logging and lumber sector, annnounced in October it was putting itself up for sale. Its current market capitalization is around C$630 million.
The sale effort was prompted by Fletcher's decision to sharpen its focus on its paper business further and a view held by both companies that TimberWest stock was undervalued.
In the first weeks after the sale decision was announced, Fletcher and TimberWest announced they had received more than 20 expressions of interest.
None of the potential buyers has been publicly identified. Analysts have speculated that bidders might include Avenor Inc which owns 51 percent of Pacific Forest Products Ltd in British Columbia.
Other names mentioned by analysts were Donohue Inc, Riverside Forest Products Ltd, West Fraser Timber Co Ltd and Slocan Forest Products.

Weyerhaeuser Co and Champion International Corp were listed as potential U.S. buyers. In addition, the timberland investment management division of U.S. insurer John Hancock Mutural Life Insurance Co may have an interest in TimberWest, analysts said.

The firm bills itself as the world's largest timberland investment manager and last year bought 13,000 hectares of British Columbia timberland from Weldwood of Canada Ltd. TimberWest has five sawmills in British Columbia with annual capacity of 685 million board feet of lumber. It also has timber tenures with annual harvest of 4.2 million cubic meters of wood including 210,000 hectares of privately owned land on the British Columbia coast.

The sale is subject to approval by the British Columbia forest ministry which last year blocked Canfor Corp's takeover bid for Slocan on the grounds it would have created too much concentration in the coastal forest industry.
That has led some analysts to believe it would be unlikely for a coastal forest company to succeed in buying TimberWest.
